messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P99 TLS handshake tail latency spike detected in eu-west-2 (AZ-B <-> AZ-C). Metric snapshot: p99_handshake_ms=1200ms, p95_token_ms=320ms. Affected routes: streaming.*. Incident ID INC-2026-0412-01. Auto-threshold triggered at 07:12UTC.
michelle: Paging on-call. @sam you up?
sam: on-call here, just saw PD. Pulling traces and tcpdumps now.
raj: I'm seeing packet loss counters tick up on the VXLAN hop between AZ-B and AZ-C, ~2-3% short windows. DNS timeouts showing for model-catalog on same zone pair.
oliver: customers are reporting streaming stalls and reconnects, client logs show TLS handshake timeouts then reconnect storms.
michelle: Severity? customer impact? any Dedicated tenants affected?
sam: prelim: ~7% requests in eu-west-2 saw retries, p99 doubled. No full outage but SLOs breached for p99 handshake.
ops-bot: /runbook start interzone-network-latency — initiated by sam. Steps: confirm inter-AZ path, try local egress pref, scale proxies, escalate to netinfra.
sam: running quick tcpdump on model-proxy in AZ-B: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -w /tmp/handshake.pcap port 443 and host 10.12.34.56` — capturing SYN/SYN-ACK/TLS.
raj: tcpdump extract: SYN->SYN/ACK delayed ~800ms, retransmission seen. Also TLS ClientHello retrans. `mtr` shows packet loss at hop 6 (10.200.0.1) between AZ-B and AZ-C.
elaine: double-checking route tables and NAT gateways now: running `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Service,Values=streaming` and `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways`.
oliver: Can we prefer same-AZ egress for streaming to avoid hairpin? That would avoid cross-AZ NAT.
sam: quick mitigation: prefer local NAT by shifting proxy egress for the group — will modify service routing rules. Doing dry-run first: `aws ec2 modify-network-interface-attribute --network-interface-id eni-0abc123 --attachment AttachmentId=attach-xxx --no-dry-run` (planning to target canary).
michelle: meanwhile notify CS for high-throughput tenants in eu-west-2. @elaine please list top-10 tenants by qps and start impact notes.
elaine: on it. Dashboard shows Tenant-A, Tenant-B, Tenant-C with elevated reconnects. Drafting breach notice.
raj: digging deeper — looks like NAT ephemeral ports on nat-b spike when flows hairpin; TIME_WAIT explosion. `ss -s` shows many TIME_WAIT sockets.
sam: ephemeral port exhaustion is plausible. Short-fix: move proxies to local AZ NAT (started), scale proxy workers to increase socket pool, rolling restart of proxy group (canary).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart of service streaming-proxy in eu-west-2 starting az-b canary (10% -> 50%). Triggered by sam.
michelle: tagging netinfra — @netinfra please confirm if provider-side interconnect maintenance or flaps.
netinfra: investigating. We see ECMP asymmetry on one external peering node in eu-west-2. Provider flagged a noisy port, working on reroute. Packet drops ~1-3% on that path.
sam: mitigation plan: 1) roll proxies to prefer local NAT (in progress) 2) scale streaming proxies + increase socket limits 3) if provider confirms, cutover streaming traffic to AZ-D path 4) upload pcap to provider ticket and escalate.
oliver: customer impact summary: streaming sessions can stall 3-8s, some clients reconnect. SLO p99 handshake breach since ~07:12UTC.
elaine: sent first customer update at 07:29UTC: "We are investigating increased tail latency in eu-west-2 impacting streaming sessions. Engineers working on mitigations. Will update every 15 minutes."
sam: uploading pcap for provider: `/usr/local/bin/s3-uploader /tmp/handshake.pcap s3://inc-uploads/1801204321.pcap` and attaching to provider ticket with topology notes.
raj: after canary roll, I'm seeing p99_handshake_ms drop from ~1200ms -> ~480ms for the canaried shard. p95s are largely stable.
michelle: keep rollouts slow. If p99 < 300ms for 2 scans, we can escalate to resolved->monitoring.
netinfra: provider acknowledged and applied reroute. Expect visible improvement in 8-12 minutes while BGP converges.
ops-bot: incident log update: state=mitigating, owner=sam, started=1801204321.
sam: handing on-call to @oliver for next 30min — notes: canary at 10->50%, NAT pref updated in service config, pcap uploaded to ticket, provider engaged.
oliver: taking over. Watching p99 and reconnect metrics. Ping me for escalation.
elaine: second customer update sent at 07:41UTC with mitigation notes and expected resolution window.
michelle: postmortem TODOs: why traffic hairpinned cross-AZ, NAT ephemeral growth root cause, add provider maintenance detection to health-alerts, and validate proxy egress locality by default.
netinfra: provider reports reroute effective. Observed p99_handshake_ms settling ~150-220ms. Continuing 30m watch.
oliver: monitoring looks good. Will keep for 30m then move to resolved->monitoring if stable.
ops-bot: incident state change requested by oliver: state=resolved, resolved_by=oliver, resolved_ts=1801207899. Summary: cross-AZ packet loss on provider path caused TLS handshake tail spikes; mitigation via local NAT preference + proxy rolling canary + provider reroute.
michelle: thanks all. Please add timeline and links to pcaps/graphs in the postmortem doc.
